Scope it yourself

Twelve questions, two minutes.

For the person who wants to be specific before they are ready to talk to anyone. You end up with a summary you can copy, circulate internally, or send to us — and if you send it, the conversation starts two steps further along.

Or just write to us

Start here

Every answer stays in your browser. There is no submit until the end and no field asking who you are.

1 of 12What does the business do?
2 of 12How many people in total?
3 of 12How many would actually use the system daily?
4 of 12How many locations?
5 of 12What runs the business today?
6 of 12What made you look?
7 of 12How clean is your existing data, honestly?
8 of 12How much history has to come across?
9 of 12Which of these apply?
10 of 12What do you think you need?
11 of 12When would you want to be live?
12 of 12Who decides?

Twelve questions, about two minutes. Nothing is sent anywhere until you choose to send it.

Your scope, as far as you have described it

Send it to us
Copied to your clipboard, and carried into the enquiry form if you send it. We have not received anything yet — this all happened in your browser.


What we do with it
If you send it, it arrives as an enquiry with the answers attached, and the scope that comes back is more specific because of it. If you do not, nothing has happened — no cookie, no record, no follow-up.
The questions are the ones we would ask on a first call anyway. Answering them here does not commit you to the call; it just means the call is thirty minutes instead of an hour.


Or skip the form entirely.
Five lines of email works just as well. "We are forty people selling building materials and our stock numbers are never right" is a perfectly good brief.
